name: Kasih Turtle Conservation Project
summary: Beach hatchery at Pantai Chendor that carries on Paksu Cherating’s work: getting turtle eggs back into the sand instead of onto plates, then releasing the hatchlings.
programmes: Daily hatchling releases in season, open to visitors
Merch sales to fund the hatchery
Partner events such as corporate mangrove planting and beach clean-ups
beneficiaries: Sea turtles nesting at Pantai Chendor, Cherating, Pahang; visitors

live.note: Hatchling releases at dusk are the natural live moment. Nesting season is ending: Kasih stopped advance release bookings from 5 October 2026.

donationsToday: Not published. Contact through Instagram or WhatsApp.
background: Kasih describes itself as the continuation of Paksu Cherating’s turtle-egg work (Rimbun Dahan Turtle Hatchery). The New Straits Times profiled Pak Su, Ariffin Hassan, in November 2018; his son Fadhil Izzudin Ariffin later took over the Chendor hatchery. Kasih’s link to the family is not yet confirmed.
